original_question: Which pair of prelaminations forces any group action that preserves it to induce an Ansov-like action on the corresponding bifoliated plane?
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact target almost verbatim: it asks about a pair of prelaminations, requires a universal implication for every preserving group action, and asks for the induced action on the associated bifoliated plane to be Anosov-like. The main issue is that the paper states this question informally and leaves the ambient circle-action setup implicit. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient objects should be stated explicitly: the prelaminations are prelaminations on S^1, where a lamination on S^1 is a closed subset of ((S^1 × S^1 - Δ)/(x,y) ∼ (y,x)) with pairwise unlinked elements, and a prelamination is the same notion without the closedness condition. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The phrase "any group action that preserves it" should be unpacked as: for any action of a group G on S^1 that preserves both prelaminations in the pair setwise. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The phrase "the corresponding bifoliated plane" is implicit in the paper and should be made explicit as the bifoliated plane associated to the preserved pair of prelaminations via the Barthelmé-Bonatti-Mann viewpoint invoked immediately before Question 6.5. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The intended task is classificatory: determine exactly which pairs of prelaminations have this universal forcing property, not merely provide one sufficient example. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Terminology should be normalized to "Anosov-like"; the printed Question 6.5 has a typo ("Ansov-like"), but the surrounding discussion repeatedly uses "Anosov-like." ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic-quantifier data are relevant here; the omitted data are topological and dynamical rather than algebraic. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Characterize the pairs (Λ+, Λ-) of prelaminations on S^1 with the following property: for every group action ρ: G → Homeo(S^1) that preserves both Λ+ and Λ-, the induced action of G on the bifoliated plane associated to (Λ+, Λ-) is Anosov-like.
justification: The draft matches Question 6.5 in Section 6.3 essentially word-for-word, so that is the nearest official formulation. The nearby context in the same subsection supplies the needed hidden assumptions: it defines lamination/prelamination on S^1, recalls the motivating special case of a cofinite action with a veering pair of invariant laminations and no crown gaps that induces an Anosov-like action, and then says that Question 6.5 is an intentionally informal translation via the work of Barthelmé-Bonatti-Mann. The refined version therefore only makes explicit the ambient circle action, the meaning of preserving the pair, and the association to a bifoliated plane, without broadening beyond the paper. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
